image_class_embeds.description: Per-patch visual embedding in the shared cross-modal 512-d space (output of class_head.dense0 from image_embeds after vision_model+cls-token-broadcast+layer_norm)

text_embeds.description: Per-prompt text embedding in the same shared 512-d space (output of owlvit.text_projection from text_model pooled output)

logit_shift.description: Per-patch additive logit bias (output of class_head.logit_shift)

logit_scale.description: Per-patch multiplicative logit scale (output of class_head.logit_scale, ELU+1 applied, always positive)

normalization_step.code_line_256_257:
image_class_embeds = image_class_embeds / (torch.linalg.norm(image_class_embeds, dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
query_embeds = query_embeds / (torch.linalg.norm(query_embeds, dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
normalization_step.description: L2-normalize both image_class_embeds and text_embeds (query_embeds is the local alias for text_embeds in decode()) along the 512-d embedding dimension. The 1e-6 epsilon prevents division by zero. This converts both to unit hypersphere -- making the next step a COSINE similarity (dot product of unit vectors = cosine of angle).

similarity_computation.description: Einstein summation: for each (batch b, patch p, text_query n), compute the dot product of the normalized 512-d embeddings. Since both are unit-normalized this is EXACTLY cosine similarity. Output shape [B, 576, N] -- for each of 576 patch locations in each of B images, a raw similarity score against each of N text prompts.

logit_transform.description: Apply the per-patch learned additive shift s_{b,p} and per-patch learned multiplicative scale \tau_{b,p}. This is NOT a single global temperature like CLIP's exp(logit_scale); every one of 576 locations has its OWN shift and scale, learned end-to-end. The shift can be negative (bias term) and the scale is always >0 (ELU(x)+1). Broadcasting: logit_shift and logit_scale are [B,576,1], the 1 broadcasts across the N text-query dimension.

sigmoid_to_score.description: Sigmoid function converts unbounded logits into [0,1] scores. This is NOT a softmax across categories (which would force competition); sigmoid is applied independently per (b,p,n) -- each patch+text-query pair gets a binary-classification-style score in [0,1]. Multi-label, not mutually-exclusive.

equation_derivation.final_equation_expanded: score_{b,p,n} = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\Big(-\tau_{b,p} \cdot \big(\cos(\theta(v_{b,p}, t_n)) + s_{b,p}\big)\Big)}, where \cos(\theta) is the cosine similarity of L2-normalized embeddings

threshold_and_argmax_decode.code_lines_262_268: scores_max = scores_sigmoid.max(dim=-1); labels = scores_max.indices; scores = scores_max.values; ...
threshold_and_argmax_decode.description: For each (b,p), take argmax over the N text queries to get the best-matching label index and its score. Then apply threshold masking: only patches where (label==target AND score>threshold) survive. The surviving (b,p) slots emit their corresponding pred_boxes[b,p] (from the box_head branch) as detections. This is how 576 per-patch predictions collapse into a sparse set of actual object detections.
threshold_and_argmax_decode.note: This argmax+threshold decode is NOT part of the cross-modal similarity equation itself, but is the detection-decoding policy. The equation ends at score_{b,p,n}; the rest is post-processing.

comparison_to_clip.clip_global_image_text: CLIP: whole-image embedding v_global \in R^d, text t \in R^d, both L2-normalized, similarity = v_global \cdot t, scaled by a SINGLE GLOBAL learned scalar temperature parameter, passed through softmax(categories) for classification.
comparison_to_clip.owlvit_per_patch: OWL-ViT: PER-PATCH embedding v_{b,p} \in R^{512}, text t_n \in R^{512}, both L2-normalized, similarity = v_{b,p} \cdot t_n + PER-PATCH shift s_{b,p}, scaled by PER-PATCH scale \tau_{b,p}, passed through SIGMOID (multi-label, not softmax). 576 independent (patch, text) similarity scores per image. Each patch also emits a bbox prediction from box_head. Detection = high-scoring patch + its box.
comparison_to_clip.key_difference: CLIP has ONE image representation (CLS token); OWL-ViT has 576 per-patch representations (via the cls_token * patch_tokens element-wise multiplication that injects global context into every patch, turning the single global representation into 576 local-global-fused representations suitable for DETECTION). OWL-ViT's class_head (dense0 + logit_shift + logit_scale) is the per-patch analog of CLIP's image_projection + single logit_scale temperature, but learned per-location.

no_background_class_head.observation: There is NO separate 'background' class or explicit background embedding in the text_embeds tensor. The sigmoid(logit) produces a [0,1] score; low scores (<threshold) are implicitly treated as 'not this object here', but there is no trainable background embedding competing with the foreground text prompts. This is different from Faster R-CNN-style two-stage detectors that have an explicit background class in the classifier head.

bias_in_projections.class_head_dense0: Linear(768->512, bias=True) -- YES, additive bias in the image-side projection.
bias_in_projections.text_projection: Inherited from CLIP CLIPTextProjection, typically Linear(512->512, bias=False by default in transformers CLIP implementation) -- need to check actual loaded model's state_dict to confirm bias presence, but CLIP convention is no-bias in text_projection.
bias_in_projections.impact: If text_projection has no bias, the text embedding is a pure linear projection of the pooled hidden state. If class_head.dense0 has bias, the image embedding has a learned additive offset before normalization. Both are normalized to unit-sphere anyway, so the bias only shifts the PRE-NORMALIZATION distribution -- post-normalization both are on the hypersphere and the bias's main effect is captured in the direction (not magnitude) of the projected vector.
